claim_findings.basis_reference: Question premise: "A proof claims that sqrt(2) is rational: write sqrt(2)=a/b in lowest terms, square to get a^2=2b^2, and conclude that a and b are both even."
Definitions of rationality, evenness, and divisibility.
Well-ordering principle for positive integers: every nonempty set of positive integers has a least member; applied in steps least-denominator and parity-decomposition.
Derived from the well-ordering principle in step parity-decomposition.
Temporary negation of the intended conclusion that sqrt(2) is irrational.
Derived in steps rational-representation through lowest-terms-property from the local rationality assumption and the well-ordering principle.
Derived by squaring the least-denominator representation in step square-equation.
Derived in steps a-square-even and a-even using the parity dichotomy.
Derived in steps substitute-a through b-even using the parity dichotomy.
Derived in step lowest-terms-conflict from the least-denominator property and the evenness of a and b.
Reductio in step conclude-irrational, after discharge of the local rationality assumption at lowest-terms-conflict.

objection_history.attack: The argument assumes a lowest-terms integer representation, which is available only if sqrt(2) is rational; it cannot directly establish rationality.
Test whether the lowest-terms assumption is actually discharged by a contradiction.
Check the parity inference: an even square implies an even integer only after an exhaustive parity theorem is established.
Check whether contradiction of one assumed lowest-terms representation proves that sqrt(2) is irrational.
The quoted premise might already establish rationality rather than only describe a claimed proof.
Check whether the least-denominator construction assumes a representation before rationality has been assumed.
Check whether squaring or multiplying by b^2 divides by zero.
Check whether an even square necessarily implies an even integer.
Check whether substitution yields b^2=2c^2 without an invalid cancellation.
Check whether 2 is a prohibited common divisor and whether the reductio scope is discharged.
Check whether the conclusion is inferred only after the temporary rationality assumption is discharged.
